problem: What is the sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series if the first term is $3$ and the common ratio is $15?$
worked_solution:
The sum of the first $N$ terms of a geometric series can be determined by the formula

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{{a}_{1}(1-{r}^{N})}{1-r}.
$$

In this case, ${a}_{1}=3$ and $r=15.$ Therefore, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{S}_{N} & =\frac{3(1-{15}^{N})}{1-15} \\  & =-\frac{3}{14}(1-{15}^{N}) \\  & =\frac{3}{14}({15}^{N}-1)\end{aligned}
$$
